text:
Berkly Catton is why people are watching the Kraken. His first NHL hat trick, in a 5-1 win over Vancouver, was a moment NDTV Sports called Kraken history, and he has 9 points in his last 10 games against 5.6 expected. His line with Kaapo Kakko and Shane Wright is roughly even on chances (51%), a good sign for a group that young.

Underneath that, Seattle is harder to trust. The Kraken are 11-9-1 after Monday's 3-2 win over Anaheim, but they have only 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 45% at 5-on-5. They've scored about seven more goals than those chances predict, and our standings model has them three points ahead of their play.

The penalty kill is the sore spot. After Saturday's 4-3 loss in San Jose, with two power-play goals against, coach Lane Lambert called it "the elephant in the room," per the Kraken's Alison Lukan. Matty Beniers had scored in three straight by then.

The veteran line of Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann gets just 39% of the expected goals, and McMann has 2 points in 10 against 5.1 expected. Adam Larsson and Vince Dunn take 39% of the shot attempts. The roster churned too: Jagger Firkus debuted in the Global Series finale before going back to Coachella Valley, and Jani Nyman was sent down.

Our playoff odds have Seattle at 36%. What we'd watch: whether the young forwards take more of the hard minutes from the veterans.
headline: Catton's breakout, and a penalty kill that worries
